title: High-order quantum correlations in nonlinear waveguide quantum electrodynamics
authors: I Gusti Ngurah Yudi Handayana, Ya-Tang Yu, C. -Y. Lee, K. -T. Lin, G. -D. Lin, H. H. Jen
abstract: Quantum emitters coupled to nonlinear one-dimensional waveguides provide a route for quantum-state engineering by utilizing parametric gain accumulation along with modified waveguide-mediated interactions. Since the accumulated squeezing depends on propagation distance, different emitter separations can experience different effective gain, making the spatial structure of connected quantum correlations a central feature of the dynamics. Here we investigate the transient and steady-state connected correlations of emitter arrays coupled to a parametrically driven waveguide. Using an effective master equation for nonlinear waveguide QED, we analyze second- and third-order connected correlations as functions of the squeezing parameter and interparticle distance. In the two-emitter limit, accumulated squeezing drives excitation buildup and generates a nonzero connected second-order correlation. For many-emitter arrays, tuning the interparticle distance switches the dominant local second-order correlation between the bulk and boundary regions, and enables an analogous spatial control of genuine third-order connected correlations. In the steady state, the averaged second-order correlation exhibits sign-changing and nonmonotonic behavior in the squeezing--interparticle distance parameter space, whereas the third-order connected correlation is strongly enhanced by increasing the squeezing parameter. These results identify nonlinear waveguide QED as a tunable platform for spatially controlling connected quantum correlations and provide insights into correlation engineering in open quantum optical arrays. We further show that this local contrast remains visible in both odd and even number of atomic arrays.
summary: This paper explores the generation and spatial control of high-order quantum correlations in an array of emitters coupled to a nonlinear waveguide. By analyzing second- and third-order connected correlations using an effective master equation, the authors show that tuning emitter spacing allows for switching between bulk and boundary correlation dominance. This establishes nonlinear waveguide QED as a versatile platform for engineering complex quantum states.
main_problem: The study investigates how high-order quantum correlations (second- and third-order) are generated and controlled in an array of emitters coupled to a nonlinear waveguide.
main_result: The research demonstrates that the system allows for tunable spatial control over connected quantum correlations by manipulating interparticle distance, and shows strong enhancement of third-order correlations with increasing squeezing.
method: The analysis employs an effective master equation derived from nonlinear waveguide QED to track transient and steady-state correlation functions.
model_or_system: The system consists of $N$ two-level emitters coupled linearly to a one-dimensional, parametrically driven nonlinear waveguide. The dynamics are governed by an effective master equation incorporating excitation exchange and squeezing-induced pair terms.
key_observables: Second-order and third-order connected correlations ($G^{(2)}, G^{(3)}$), local boundary–bulk contrast in correlations.
important_parameters: Squeezing parameter ($r$), nearest-neighbor distance ($\Delta x$), interparticle distance, and the number of emitters ($N$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes an ideal guided-mode limit for the waveguide and focuses on the pure squeezing-accumulation regime.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates $N$ emitters coupled to a nonlinear waveguide, highlighting how near-boundary correlations arise from asymmetric contributions versus balanced bulk contributions.
paper_structure: The paper develops the effective master equation for the system, analyzes the two-emitter limit as a benchmark, and then extends the analysis to many-emitter arrays to show spatial control over local correlations by tuning interparticle distance.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses correlation engineering in open quantum optical arrays, providing concrete mechanisms (via nonlinear coupling and geometry) to manipulate higher-order quantum statistics.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic of an array of N two-level emitters coupled to a nonlinear one-dimensional waveguide. Each emitter has ground state |g⟩, excited state |e⟩, and transition frequency ω0. The emit- ters couple to the guided-mode continuum, giving rise to the guided decay rate γ under the Markov approximation. A classical pump at frequency ωp ≃2ω induces broadband parametric gain for guided field fluctuations around the signal frequency ω. The dimensionless interatomic distance is ϕ = k0∆x, where k0 is the guided-mode wavenumber evaluated at the emitter transition frequency and ∆x is the nearest-neighbor distance.
